findings.text: _operator_operand breaks the operand phrase on any stopword once one token is kept, so 'averaged over the volume of the plasma' yields the head noun 'of' and two operands sharing a head noun ('a closed flux surface' and 'the plasma surface' both reduce to 'surface') are never flagged; the operator class therefore both misses real operand differences and can emit a nonsense operand (probe run at head: operands ('surface','surface') and ('of','volume') with no operator flag).

_detect_qualifier treats the token-longer head as the agreed form with no modal or majority check, unlike the operator, convention and unit_basis detectors that call _modal; one member carrying an extra qualifier therefore flags and proposes repairs on every sibling, changing the majority toward a minority (probe at head: three identical members flagged and repaired when a single member added 'local').

verify() checks only that the page exists, never that the committed page equals render(record); at aa6e70abe render() would append the GATE_REVISION stale sentence, and the committed HTML contains no such sentence, so the page is hand-edited relative to its generator and a regeneration produces a different page with no gate catching the drift.

The done_when's acceptance measure, a blind adjudication of a seeded 20-family sample before and after (no member sound before adjudicated wrong after, and the count of adjudicated inconsistencies falling), is not performed or recorded; the page's Blind adjudication section states it is outstanding, so the section's own acceptance criterion is unproven and promotion must not read this node as accepted.

Six of the nine delivered files (this module, its test, the evidence JSON, the packet, the sealed key and the evidence generator) sit outside the two declared write paths; the section's done_when requires them, so the change is in scope for the section, but the declared scope under-specifies it and a scope audit keyed on the declared paths would read this as a breach.

_FAMILY_MEMBERS_QUERY and _GROUP_FAMILIES_QUERY re-implement parent-based family reads that iter_codex/standard_names/families.py already owns (fetch_pattern_family / _FAMILY_BASE_QUERY); the new module should reuse or extend that owner rather than fork its own HAS_PARENT query text.
